title: Snub-Poemed
subtitle: A calligram, after the Lysippos bust of Socrates
author: Johannes Sigil
composition_date_approx: Date contemporary with Sigil's working period
visual_subject: First-century Roman copy of the Lysippos bust of Socrates
license: Reserved by Johannes Sigil / Lee Sharks; included in the Mandala Oracle architecture under the heteronym's own attribution
constitutional_role: Sigil's self-portrait. The face of the underworld guide. First canonical text of the Mandala Oracle's canon — appropriately, since the witness encounters the guide before encountering the territory the guide will lead them through. The work is also the guide's own primary work; the boundary between the guide and the canon is here intentionally porous.
intertextual_layers: Socratic aphorisms (e.g. 'the same poet composing both tragedy and comedy', Symposium)
Platonic dialogue references ('satyr' from Alcibiades' speech, 'the philosopher is a dog' from Cynic reception)
First-person articulations of Platonic philosophy ('is it madness to feel and to know?')
Lyricized renditions blurring the speaker-Socrates boundary ('awkward with longing')
Self-citation: Sigil's own poetry (mis)attributed to Socrates, woven into intertext 'without indication of where one ends and the other begins'
title_pun: The title puns on Socrates' characteristic description as 'snub-nosed,' simultaneously naming the act of 'poeming' (composing) and the act of 'snubbing' (refusing). 'Snub-poemed' is what the bust has been done to: it has been remade as poem. It is also what poetry does to the bust: receptively snubs it, refuses to leave it as it was.
lysippos_maxim: Other artists make men as they are. I make them as they appear.
status: CANONICAL — Sigil's primary work, ready for star-positioning when the canon-as-sky layer is built.
